newsitem.title: UK: Cold snap boosts oil, but doubts over rally persist.
newsitem.headline: Cold snap boosts oil, but doubts over rally persist.

text.p: World oil prices rose on Monday after Arctic weather spilled down into much of Europe and the northeastern United States.
But the gains generated swift selling amid signs that worldwide stocks of crude and refined products might be on the rise, albeit from low levels.
After a solid 30 cent rally in the morning, benchmark December Brent futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange finished just four cents up on the day at $23.02 a barrel.
Monday's modest rise followed a blistering 77-cent rally on Friday.
"Prices were always likely to rally at the first true signs of winter cold, and this is what we are seeing at the moment," brokers GNI in London said.
But traders said rising stocks of crude and heating oil in Europe and the U.S. may take the steam out of the market.
"EU gas oil (heating oil) stocks are expected to rise in October, which is worth noting," one said.
"There is not an awful lot of stock around, but I get the impression that there is enough," he added.
Market analysts said they expected Tuesday's report from the Euroilstock Foundation to show a modest build in October of European oil stocks, including distillates such as heating oil.
Low heating oil stocks, along with Middle Eastern tension and strong demand, helped lift crude to near six-year highs of $25.06 in mid-October.
It has since retraced sharply to as low as $22.11 before recovering during the last two trading days.
